title: Matthias (Acts 1:15–26)
hookLine: they pray, cast lots, and the twelfth place is filled

lines: A HUNDRED AND TWENTY IN PRAYER.
cards: Every team photo with an empty spot has a story. A chair left empty at the table, a name missing from the roster. Someone has to decide whether to fill it, and how.

After the Ascension the disciples go back to an upper room in Jerusalem and pray together, about a hundred and twenty of them, Luke says, with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus. There were twelve apostles.
Now there are eleven. And Peter, only weeks after his own worst failure, stands up to deal with the empty chair.

teach.b: Peter speaks about Judas plainly and without gloating: he was numbered with us and had a share in this ministry. Then he gives the qualifications for the empty place.

It has to be someone who was with them the whole time, from John's baptism to the day Jesus was taken up, someone who can be a witness with them of the resurrection. Yesterday's word, witness, as the job description.

Two men fit: Joseph called Barsabas, also known as Justus, and Matthias. Both, we're told, were there from the start, and Acts tells us nothing more about either one. Then they do two things, in this order.
First they pray, saying: Lord, you who know the hearts of all, show which of these two you have chosen.
Then they cast lots, something like drawing straws. In the Douay-Rheims: "And they gave them lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles."
Casting lots was an old way in Israel of leaving a decision to God; Proverbs says the lot is cast, but the decision is the Lord's.
Some readers notice that once the Spirit comes at Pentecost, Acts shows the apostles deciding in other ways, by prayer, discussion and the Spirit's lead. What stays is the order: they prayed first.
And Matthias, chosen by a falling lot, is honored by the Church as an apostle.
Faithful from the beginning, and Acts never names him again.

how: Catholics keep a feast of Saint Matthias, Apostle, and the Church often begins important choices, like a papal conclave, with a Mass asking the Holy Spirit's guidance.

o: the apostle who later wrote a Gospel
the man chosen by lot for the twelfth place
the disciple who replaced Peter as leader

games.q: the twelfth place — tap the pairs.

s: the apostles cast lots and then prayed about the result
they prayed first, then cast lots.
Peter's test for the empty place was being with them from the beginning
from John's baptism to the day Jesus was taken up.
Acts tells us a great deal about what Matthias did next
after he is chosen, Acts never names him again.

games.q: you're Peter. there's an empty place among the twelve, and two good men who fit. how do you choose?
o: they wait for Jesus to return.
games.why: they pray, asking the Lord who knows all hearts to show his choice, then cast lots, and the lot falls on Matthias.

practice: Bring to mind a decision in front of you, large or small: a job, a conversation, a purchase, where to spend Saturday.
Hold the options side by side, the way the apostles held two names, and don't decide yet; just breathe with them there together.
If you pray, borrow the apostles' request in your own words, asking God, who knows the heart, to show you; if you don't, simply hold the options in quiet.

wordCard.voice: Matthias. Chosen after prayer and the casting of lots to take the twelfth place among the apostles. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: lot, also a share or portion; it gives English the word clergy.

carryVoice: Your line: they prayed first. Prayer, then the choice, always in that order. Until tomorrow.
